([[Colorado Springs, Colorado]]) | college = [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]] (2008–2011) | draft_year = 2011 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 24 | draft_team = [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] | career_start = 2011 | years1 = {{nbay|2011|start}}–{{nbay|2014|end}} | team1 = [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] | years2 = {{nbay|2014|end}}–{{nbay|2019|end}} | team2 = [[Detroit Pistons]] | years3 = {{nbay|2019|end}}–{{nbay|2022|end}} | team3 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | years4 = {{nbay|2022|end}}–{{nbay|2023|end}} | team4 = [[Denver Nuggets]] | years5 = {{nbay|2024|full=y}} | team5 = [[Philadelphia 76ers]] | highlights = * [[List of NBA champions|NBA champion]] ([[2023 NBA Finals|2023]]) * First-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2011) * [[Mr. Colorado Basketball]] (2008) }} '''Reginald Shon Jackson''' (born April 16, 1990),{{cite web|first=Frank|last=Dell'Apa|title=This nest best; Eagles' Jackson thinks he chose right place|url=http://archive.boston.com/sports/colleges/mens_basketball/articles/2010/12/25/eagles_jackson_thinks_he_found_the_best_nest_at_boston_college/|work=Boston Globe|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140501074823/http://www.boston.com/sports/colleges/mens_basketball/articles/2010/12/25/eagles_jackson_thinks_he_found_the_best_nest_at_boston_college/?page=full|archive-date=May 1, 2014|date=December 25, 2010|url-status=live}} nicknamed '''Big Government''' and '''Mr. June''', is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played three seasons for the [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College Eagles]] before declaring for the [[2011 NBA draft]], where he was drafted 24th overall by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. Jackson has also played for the [[Detroit Pistons]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], and [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. In 2023, Jackson won a championship with the [[Denver Nuggets]]. ==Early life== Jackson was born in [[Pordenone]], in northeast [[Italy]], to American parents.{{cite web|url=http://newsok.com/okc-thunder-the-around-the-world-travels-of-reggie-jackson/article/3917788|title=OKC Thunder: The around-the-world travels of Reggie Jackson|work=NewsOK.com}} His father served at [[Aviano Air Base]]. The Jacksons later moved to [[England]] before going to the United States when Jackson was five. The family lived in [[North Dakota]] for a year before moving to [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] and [[Florida]] before settling in [[Colorado Springs, Colorado]] when Jackson was in the sixth grade.{{cite web|title=Player Bio: Reggie Jackson|url=http://www.bceagles.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/reggie_jackson_359790.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131114003939/http://www.bceagles.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/reggie_jackson_359790.html|archive-date=November 14, 2013|access-date=October 28, 2011|publisher=Boston College Official Athletic Site}} He graduated from [[General William J. Palmer High School]] in Colorado Springs in 2008, and won the 2007–08 Gatorade Colorado Boys' Basketball Player of the Year. In April 2008, Jackson officially declared as an American citizen and relinquished his Italian citizenship.{{cite web|last=Weinstein|first=Jeff|title=Freshman Focus: Meet Reggie Jackson|url=http://www.bceagles.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111008aad.html|publisher=Boston College Eagles|access-date=April 26, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120117175714/http://www.bceagles.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111008aad.html|archive-date=January 17, 2012}} Considered a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Jackson was listed as the No. 29 shooting guard and the No. 115 player in the nation in 2008.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Reggie-Jackson-67527|title=Reggie Jackson}} ==College career== [[File:Reggie Jackson Boston College.jpg|thumb|150px|left|Jackson with Boston College]] Jackson arrived at [[Boston College]] and joined a team that was already armed with stars such as [[Tyrese Rice]] and [[Rakim Sanders]]. In Jackson's freshman season, the Eagles made the NCAA tournament with Jackson being used as an explosive weapon off the bench. In his second season, Jackson stepped into a starting role following the departure of Rice, but the Eagles were unable to make it back to the NCAA Tournament. As a junior in [[2010–11 Boston College Eagles men's basketball team|2010–11]], Jackson led the Eagles in scoring with 18.2 points per game and led them to the [[National Invitation Tournament]].{{cite web |url=http://bceagles.cstv.com/auto_pdf/p_hotos/s_chools/bc/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/cumulative-stats |title=Cumulative stats |publisher=Boston College Official Athletic Site |access-date=October 28, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110908142519/http://bceagles.cstv.com/auto_pdf/p_hotos/s_chools/bc/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/cumulative-stats |archive-date=September 8, 2011 }} He subsequently earned first-team All-ACC honors alongside [[Nolan Smith]], [[Jordan Williams (basketball, born 1990)|Jordan Williams]], [[Malcolm Delaney]] and [[Kyle Singler]].{{cite web |url=http://www.newsobserver.com/2011/03/07/1036739/dukes-smith-singler-named-first.html |title=Duke's Smith, Singler named first-team All-ACC |publisher=NewsObserver.com |date=March 7, 2011 |access-date=October 28, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121002131018/http://www.newsobserver.com/2011/03/07/1036739/dukes-smith-singler-named-first.html |archive-date=October 2, 2012 }} After his junior season, Jackson declared for the [[NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/boston/news/story?id=6503659|title=Boston College's Reggie Jackson to remain in NBA draft|work=ESPN.com|date=May 7, 2011|access-date=May 7, 2011}} ==Professional career== ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2011–2015)=== [[File:Reggie Jackson.jpg|thumb|right|Jackson in 2012]] Jackson was drafted with the 24th overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]] by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. Jackson saw limited action in his first season with the Thunder, averaging just 11.1 minutes over 45 games playing behind [[Russell Westbrook]] and [[Eric Maynor]]. Jackson scored over three points per game but shot only 32% from the field, and that percentage dropped to 21% when Jackson took shots beyond the arc. He did not play in any of the Thunder's 20 playoff games in [[2012 NBA playoffs|2012]] as the Thunder lost to the [[Miami Heat]] in five games in the [[2012 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]]. Jackson was assigned multiple times to the [[Tulsa 66ers]] of the [[NBA Development League]] between March and December 2012.{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Reggie-Jackson/Summary/3771|title=Reggie Jackson Player Profile, Detroit Pistons, News, Rumors, NBA Stats, NCAA Stats, D-League Stats, Game Logs, Bests, Awards – RealGM}} As a sophomore during the [[2012–13 NBA season|2012–13 season]], Jackson's minutes and production steadily increased. In Game 2 of the Thunder's first-round playoff series against the [[Houston Rockets]], starting point guard Russell Westbrook tore his meniscus and was ruled out for the rest of the season, as Jackson was promoted to a starting role. In his first career start, Jackson had 14 points, two rebounds, and an assist, helping the Thunder win Game 3. As a starter during the playoffs, Jackson averaged 15.3 points, 5.3 rebounds and 4.7 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/jacksre01/gamelog/2013/|title=Reggie Jackson 2012–13 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com}} On February 6, 2014, Jackson was chosen to compete in the 2014 [[NBA Skills Challenge|Taco Bell Skills Challenge]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/as.skills.challenge/02/06/2014-taco-bell-skills-challenge-participants-official-release/|title=All-Stars Lillard, DeRozan headline field for 2014 Taco Bell Skills Challenge|author=Official Release|date=February 7, 2014|access-date=February 7, 2014|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}} On April 26, he recorded a career-high 32 points along with nine rebounds against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in game 4 of the [[2014 NBA playoffs|2014 first-round playoff]] series, which the Thunder won 92–89. Jackson had five points in the final minute of regulation to force overtime, but heaved a shot from full court, still with four seconds left. In overtime, Jackson hit four free throws to ensure a Thunder victory. He was praised for his performance as the Thunder's star players [[Kevin Durant]] and Russell Westbrook had off shooting nights.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140426/OKCMEM/gameinfo.html|title=Thunder beat Grizzlies 92–89 in OT, tie up series|date=April 27, 2014|access-date=April 27, 2014|first=Teresa|last=Walker|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}} On November 11, 2014, Jackson scored a season-high 29 points on 12-of-21 shooting in the 78–85 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141111/OKCMIL/gameinfo.html|title=Mayo, Knight help Bucks hold off Thunder, 85–78|date=November 12, 2014|access-date=November 12, 2014|first=Rich|last=Rovito|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}} ===Detroit Pistons (2015–2020)=== On February 19, 2015, Jackson was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] as part of a three-team deal that also involved the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-guard-reggie-jackson|title=Detroit Pistons Acquire Guard Reggie Jackson|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=February 19, 2015|access-date=February 19, 2015}} Three days later, he made his debut for the Pistons as he recorded 17 points, five rebounds, and five assists in a 106–89 victory over the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150222/WASDET/gameinfo.html|title=New-look Pistons beat Wizards 106–89|first=Dave|last=Hogg|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=February 22, 2015|access-date=February 22, 2015}} On March 17, Jackson recorded 23 points and a career-high 20 assists in a 105–95 victory over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/features/jacksons-monster-night-lifts-pistons-past-memphis-snap-10-game-skid|title=Jackson's monster night lifts Pistons past Memphis to snap 10-game skid|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|first=Keith|last=Langlois|date=March 17, 2015|access-date=March 17, 2015}} Ten days later, Jackson recorded his second career [[Double (basketball)#Triple-double|triple-double]], finishing with 26 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 111–97 victory over the [[Orlando Magic]]. Jackson became the first Pistons guard to record multiple triple-doubles in a season since [[Isiah Thomas]] during the [[1986–87 NBA season|1986–87 season]], and the first Pistons player to do so since [[Grant Hill]] during the [[1997–98 NBA season|1997–98 season]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/features/ho-hum-another-jackson-triple-double-pistons-crush-orlando|title=Ho-hum: Another Jackson triple-double as Pistons crush Orlando|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|first=Keith|last=Langlois|date=March 27, 2015|access-date=March 27, 2015}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400579366|title=Jackson has triple-double, leads Pistons over Magic 111–97|work=ESPN.com|date=March 27, 2015|access-date=March 27, 2015}} On July 20, 2015, the Pistons re-signed Jackson to a five-year, $80 million contract.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-re-sign-center-reggie-jackson|title=Detroit Pistons Re-Sign Center Reggie Jackson|date=July 20, 2015|access-date=July 20, 2015|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13204357 |title=Sources: Reggie Jackson re-signs with Pistons on 5-year, $80M contract|date=July 6, 2015|access-date=November 8, 2015|work=ESPN.com|last=Windhorst|first=Brian|authorlink=Brian Windhorst}} On November 8, he recorded a career-high 40 points in a 120–103 victory over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. He scored 26 of his 40 points in the fourth quarter, tying [[Will Bynum]]'s franchise record for the most points in a quarter.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/features/jacksons-stellar-4th-quarter-sparks-pistons-comeback-win |title=Jackson's stellar 4th quarter sparks Pistons' comeback win |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |first=Keith |last=Langlois |date=November 8, 2015 |access-date=November 8, 2015}}{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151108/DETPOR/gameinfo.html|title=Drummond leads Pistons to comeback 120–103 win over Blazers|date=November 8, 2015|access-date=November 8, 2015|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}} On December 2, Jackson had a season-best game with 34 points and 16 assists in a 127–122 overtime victory over the Phoenix Suns.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151202/PHXDET/gameinfo.html|title=Jackson rallies Pistons past Suns 127–122 in OT|date=December 2, 2015|access-date=December 2, 2015|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}} He was subsequently named the Eastern Conference [[2015–16 NBA season#Players of the week|Player of the Week]] for the week ending December 6. Jackson averaged 27.0 points and 8.8 assists, leading the Pistons to four consecutive wins during that time. Jackson became the first Piston to record 30-plus points and 15-plus assists in a game since [[Isiah Thomas]] recorded 40-plus points and 17 assists in [[1987–88 NBA season|1988]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/reggie-jackson-named-eastern-conference-player-week|title=Reggie Jackson Named Eastern Conference Player of the Week|date=December 7, 2015|access-date=December 7, 2015|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}} Jackson was named the Eastern Conference Player of the Week for the week ending December 20. He joined [[Andre Drummond]] as the only Pistons teammates to win the award twice in the same season. Jackson averaged 29.3 points (first in the Eastern Conference), 7.7 assists (second in the Eastern Conference) and 6.3 rebounds while helping lead the Pistons to a 2–1 record for the week against three teams with above .500 records. He shot 46% from the field, 38% from behind the arc and 83% from the free-throw line. Jackson recorded two 30/10 games with 34 points and a season-high 11 rebounds against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on December 14 and 31 points and 13 assists in a quadruple-overtime victory over the [[Chicago Bulls]] on December 18. He scored 13 of the Pistons' 20 points in the deciding fourth overtime period.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/reggie-jackson-named-eastern-conference-player-week-0|title=Reggie Jackson Named Eastern Conference Player of the Week|date=December 21, 2015|access-date=December 21, 2015|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}} On April 8, 2016, he had 39 points and nine assists to help the Pistons defeat the Washington Wizards and clinch a spot in the postseason for the first time since 2009.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160408/WASDET/gameinfo.html|title=Jackson scores 39 points, Pistons clinch playoff spot|date=April 8, 2016|access-date=April 9, 2016|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}} The Pistons finished the regular season as the #8-seed in the Eastern Conference with a 44–38 record. However, in their first-round series against the first-seeded Cleveland Cavaliers, the Pistons were swept 4–0. On October 10, 2016, Jackson received platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injections to treat left knee tendinosis and an ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) sprain of his right thumb. He was subsequently ruled out for six to eight weeks.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-guard-reggie-jackson-medical-update|title=Detroit Pistons Guard Reggie Jackson Medical Update|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 10, 2016|access-date=October 10, 2016}} After missing the first 21 games of the 2016–17 season, Jackson made his season debut for the Pistons on December 4, scoring 18 points in 23 minutes against the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899742|title=Ibaka lifts Magic over Jackson and Pistons 98–92|work=ESPN.com|date=December 4, 2016|access-date=December 4, 2016}} On March 6, 2017, he scored 24 of his 26 points in the second half of a 109–95 victory over the [[Chicago Bulls]]. He made all 10 of his field goal attempts after halftime.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900333|title=Jackson's big second half lifts Pistons over Bulls, 109–95|work=ESPN.com|date=March 6, 2017|access-date=March 7, 2017}} On December 26, 2017, in a game against the [[Indiana Pacers]], Jackson suffered a grade 3 right ankle sprain and was subsequently ruled out for six to eight weeks.{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/21892151|title=Pistons' Jackson out extended time with sprain|work=ESPN.com|date=December 17, 2017|access-date=May 27, 2023}}{{cite web|last=Langlois|first=Keith|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/features/after-getting-news-jackson-6-8-weeks-maybe-more-pistons-trudge-ahead-next-man|title=After getting news on Jackson – 6–8 weeks, maybe more – Pistons trudge ahead with 'next man up'|work=NBA.com|date=December 27, 2017|access-date=December 28, 2017}} He returned to action on March 20, 2018, after missing 24 games. Jackson scored seven points on 3-of-7 shooting in 15 minutes as a starter in a 115–88 victory over the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975809|title=Griffin narrowly misses triple-double, Pistons rout Suns|work=ESPN.com|date=March 20, 2018|access-date=March 20, 2018}} On February 2, 2019, Jackson scored 29 points in a 111–101 loss to the Clippers.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071448|title=Clippers rally from 25 down, beat Pistons 111–101|work=ESPN.com|date=February 2, 2019|access-date=February 22, 2019}} On February 22, he scored a season-high 32 points in a 125–122 victory over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071550|title=Pistons survive Blake Griffin's ejection, top Hawks 125–122|work=ESPN.com|date=February 22, 2019|access-date=February 22, 2019}} On February 18, 2020, Jackson was waived by the Pistons after a contract buyout agreement was reached.{{cite web|title=Detroit Pistons and Reggie Jackson Reach Buyout Agreement|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-and-reggie-jackson-reach-buyout-agreement|date=February 18, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 18, 2020}} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2020–2023)=== On February 20, 2020, Jackson signed a one-year contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web |title=L.A. Clippers Sign Guard Reggie Jackson |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/la-clippers-sign-guard-reggie-jackson |website=NBA.com |last=Kay |first=L. |access-date=February 21, 2020 |date=February 21, 2020}} On December 1, he re-signed with the Clippers.{{cite web |title=LA Clippers Re-Sign Guard Reggie Jackson |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/la-clippers-re-sign-guard-reggie-jackson |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 2, 2020 |date=December 1, 2020}} On June 18, 2021, Jackson in the starting lineup with [[Paul George]], [[Patrick Beverley]] and [[Terance Mann]] led the Clippers to their [[2021 NBA playoffs|first Western Conference Finals]] appearance. In Game 6, Jackson scored 27 points, but the Clippers lost in six games to the [[2020-21 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix Suns]]. He averaged 17.8 points, 3.2 rebounds and 3.4 assists in the postseason. On August 11, 2021, Jackson re-signed with the Clippers on a two-year contract.{{cite web |title=LA Clippers Re-Sign Reggie Jackson |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/la-clippers-re-sign-reggie-jackson |website=NBA.com |access-date=August 15, 2021 |date=August 11, 2021}} On November 23, he scored 31 points and grabbed 10 rebounds in a loss against the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web| url = https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202111230LAC.html| title = Dallas Mavericks at Los Angeles Clippers Box Score, November 23, 2021 {{!}} Basketball-Reference.com}} On December 11, Jackson scored 25 points, including a game-winning basket with 2.2 seconds left in a 106–104 victory over the [[2021-22 Orlando Magic season|Magic]].{{Cite web|url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2021/12/11/watch-reggie-jackson-drain-game-winning-jumper-clippers-beat-magic/amp/|title=Watch Reggie Jackson drain game-winning jumper, Clippers beat Magic|date=December 12, 2021}} On February 26, 2022, he scored 25 points and grabbed 8 rebounds, along with making a game-winning layup with 4.1 seconds remaining, in a narrow 111–110 victory over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web |date=February 4, 2022 |title=Clippers' Reggie Jackson: Hits game-winning shot Thursday |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-reggie-jackson-hits-game-winning-shot-thursday |access-date=May 27, 2023 |website=cbssports.com}} On November 29, 2022, Jackson scored 24 points, recorded 12 assists, and grabbed seven rebounds during a 118–112 victory over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].[https://www.cbsnews.com/losangeles/news/clippers-overcome-13-point-deficit-rally-past-blazers-for-118-112-victory/ Clippers overcome 13-point deficit, rally past Blazers for 118–112 victory] On February 9, 2023, Jackson and a future second-round pick were traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in exchange for [[Mason Plumlee]].{{Cite web |title=Hornets Acquire 2028 Second-Round Pick, Reggie Jackson And Cash Considerations From L.A. Clippers |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-acquire-2028-second-round-pick-reggie-jackson-and-cash-considerations-from-l-a-clippers |date=February 9, 2023 |accessdate=May 27, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} Three days later, Jackson and the Hornets reached a contract buyout agreement.{{Cite web |title=Hornets waive Reggie Jackson |url=https://hoopshype.com/2023/02/12/hornets-waive-reggie-jackson/ |access-date=February 12, 2023 |website=HoopsHype}} ===Denver Nuggets (2023–2024)=== On February 14, 2023, Jackson signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|title=DENVER NUGGETS SIGN REGGIE JACKSON|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-sign-reggie-jackson|website=NBA.com|date=February 14, 2023|access-date=February 15, 2023}} Jackson won his first NBA championship when the Nuggets defeated the [[Miami Heat]] in five games during the [[2023 NBA Finals]].{{Cite web |title=Nuggets take home 1st NBA title in rugged 94-89 win over Heat |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401544850 |access-date=2023-06-24 |website=ESPN |language=en}} On July 16, 2023, Jackson re-signed with the Nuggets.{{cite web|title=DENVER NUGGETS RE-SIGN REGGIE JACKSON|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-re-sign-reggie-jackson|website=NBA.com|date=July 16, 2023|access-date=July 18, 2023}} On November 27, he scored a season-high 35 points on 79% shooting, along with 13 assists, five rebounds, and two steals, leading a depleted Denver squad to a 113–104 road victory over his former team, the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|first=Farbod|last=Esnaashari|title=Unexpected Nuggets Player Makes History vs LA Clippers|url=https://www.si.com/nba/nuggets/news/unexpected-nuggets-player-makes-history-vs-la-clippers|website=SI.com|date=November 28, 2023|access-date=November 30, 2023}} On July 6, 2024, Jackson was traded by the Nuggets to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in a six-team sign and trade, which also included the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], [[Golden State Warriors]], [[Dallas Mavericks]], and [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], and the transaction became the NBA's first six-team transaction.{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Acquire Josh Green, Reggie Jackson And Two Second-Round Picks In Six-Team Trade|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-acquire-josh-green-reggie-jackson-and-two-second-round-picks-in-six-team-trade|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 7, 2024}} On July 23, he was waived by the Hornets.{{cite web|title=Hornets Waive Reggie Jackson|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-waive-reggie-jackson-2|website=NBA.com|date=July 23, 2024|access-date=July 23, 2024}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2024–2025)=== On July 30, 2024, Jackson signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers Sign Reggie Jackson|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-reggie-jackson|website=NBA.com|date=July 30, 2024|access-date=July 30, 2024}} On February 6, 2025, Jackson was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in exchange for [[Jared Butler]].{{cite web|title=Washington Acquires First-Round Pick From Philadelphia |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/washington-acquires-first-round-pick-from-philadelphia|website=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2025|access-date=February 6, 2025}} Following the trade, he was waived by Washington.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/sixers-trade-reggie-jackson-wizards|title=Wizards trade for veteran guard Reggie Jackson|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2025|quote=The Wizards have
